usage: A friendly goodbye when you expect to meet again, here addressed to a man. The verb carries the pronoun: araka to a man, araki to a woman, arakum to a group. Swap la7iqan for ghadan or qariban to say "tomorrow" or "soon".

variants.label: to a woman
variants.note: Use when speaking to a woman.

variants.label: tomorrow
variants.note: Use when the next meeting is the next day.

variants.label: soon
variants.note: Use when you do not know exactly when.

variants.label: the standard goodbye
variants.note: More formal, and works whether or not a meeting is planned.

examples.arabic: يَجِبُ أَنْ أَذْهَبَ الْآنَ، أَرَاكَ لَاحِقاً.
examples.transliteration: yajibu an adhhaba al-ana, araka la7iqan.
examples.english: I have to go now, see you later.
Thanks for the coffee, see you later.
See you all later at the meeting.
